outcome.answer:
Repeating data during pretraining often hurts performance compared with using fresh data, but the effect depends on how repetition is structured and how much unique data is available [1, 2, 3]. In controlled studies, loss can peak at an intermediate repeat count, and repeating a moderately sized subset moderately many times can be more damaging than other repeat patterns [1]. Replaying shards consecutively or concentrating repeats on fewer samples also raises loss [2]. Limited unique data causes increasingly large loss penalties for larger models [3].

Repetition is not uniformly harmful: with unique data constrained, diffusion language models can benefit from more epochs, and one reported model improved downstream performance by repeating standard pretraining data [10].
